evidence: Cic. Balb. 47: omnia jūra bellī (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: To learn completely, or by heart (Lewis & Short); the perfect perdidicī is “I have mastered”. Rare but classical. For learning in general, see learn; for mastering a feeling, see control (regere) and use vincere.

phrases.latin: locus dē mōribus est ōrātōrī perdiscendus
phrases.english: the subject of character is one the orator must master

sources: The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 338.
